differences: Movie, show, and artist details use a generic poster hero followed by disconnected cards instead of an Intercom-style bounded workspace with a calm header, primary pane, and inspector.
Operational facts, request history, files, subtitles, and status are visually equal cards rather than grouped inspector sections separated by dividers.
Season, episode, album, version, release, and history rows have useful density but lack the stronger header rails, selected-neutral controls, and pane rhythm visible in the reference.
The movie releases pane is visually separated from the detail header and facts, which weakens the sense that all controls belong to one media workspace.
At narrow widths the poster hero compresses but retains desktop card spacing and does not yet establish a clear mobile order for primary content and metadata.

A live browser baseline could not be captured because the isolated in-app browser surface was unavailable; this verdict combines the implemented source, the current shared visual tokens, and the downloaded Intercom reference corpus.
suggestions: Turn each detail page into one bordered workspace surface with a compact media header and a two-pane desktop body.
Place releases, seasons, and albums in the flexible primary pane while grouping facts, files, requests, subtitles, and history into a 320-360px inspector.
Replace floating-card spacing inside the workspace with shared one-pixel dividers and section headers.
Use neutral segmented filters and charcoal primary actions while retaining semantic chips for availability, waiting, failure, and progress.
Collapse to a single pane below tablet width, keep primary media content before inspector metadata, and preserve 44px touch targets.
reasoning: The existing implementation already exposes the real HolyArrs lifecycle and preserves strong operational density. Its visual grouping still resembles a conventional dashboard detail page. The approved references use a much stronger workspace model: a quiet header, one continuous canvas, a flexible working pane, and a dedicated inspector with divider-based groups. The implementation should keep every existing API-backed action and state while changing only the local hierarchy and styling of the three detail views.
